title: dynamic-qa Execution Profile v1
description: Strict, versioned contract for one Execution Profile file (qa/execution-profiles/<profile-id>.yaml), referenced by id from a Provenance Manifest binding record's executionProfile.id (dynamic-qa-provenance-v1.schema.json, #146). Generated before activation so a Flow's paths, commands, environments, network, identities, effects, resources, and evidence are enforceable rather than assumed (DESIGN-dynamic-qa-spec.md §5.3, SPEC-135.md user stories 40-41). A profile declares handles and policy, never secret values. Provider adapters may strengthen a profile, never omit or weaken it. This document is the human-readable contract; dynamic-qa/shared/scripts/execution-profile.mjs is the hand-written fail-closed validator that enforces it, and dynamic-qa/shared/scripts/capability-gate.mjs is the Capability Gate that checks a validated profile against actual environment evidence before activation (no JSON Schema validator dependency is added — see dynamic-qa/DECISIONS.md and the run brief's deterministic-core decision).

schema.description: Immutable. Any other value, including a plausible future version string, is an unsupported-schema-version error, not a silent upgrade attempt.

id.description: Immutable, semantic, kebab-case Execution Profile ID. Must equal the file's basename without extension. Never derived from an issue number; never reused; never renamed.

owners.description: Who approved this profile. Distinct roles per the run brief's separate-approvals invariant.

allowedPhases.description: Which safe-execution Trust Zone phases this profile may be used in (spec §11's four Trust Zones).

disposable.description: Must be true: the run must execute on disposable, unprivileged compute (SPEC-135 story 86).

disposabilityEvidence.description: How disposability is evidenced, e.g. "fresh VM per job, destroyed after".

sandbox.description: Sandbox mechanism, e.g. "os-level container", "vm", "none" (a literal "none" is a valid value; the Capability Gate, not this schema, decides if that is acceptable for a given phase).

paths.description: Both may be empty arrays (no read/write access granted), but the keys themselves are required — undeclared filesystem reach is forbidden by default, so every profile must say so explicitly.

denyProduction.description: Positive-deny production identifiers. Non-empty: a profile must name at least one production identifier it explicitly denies.

mode.description: Defaults to none. exact-allowlist requires every other field below.

origin.description: An exact origin, e.g. "https://api.example-staging.test". Wildcards ("*"), bare TLDs, or CIDR ranges broader than a single host are rejected by execution-profile.mjs as not exact.

externallyEnforced.description: True only when egress is enforced by a mechanism outside the test process itself (a network policy, egress proxy, or firewall) — never by the test code's own good behaviour. A permissive hosted runner with no such mechanism does not satisfy exact egress (SPEC-135 story 88).

network.description: network.mode="exact-allowlist" requires allowlist (non-empty), dnsRecheck, redirectRecheck, denyMetadataRange, denyInternalRange, denyPublicRange, externallyEnforced (all true), and a non-empty enforcementMechanism. execution-profile.mjs enforces this combination; this schema only shapes the fields.

handle.description: A named handle, never a secret value.

credentials.description: May be an empty object when no credential is required by this profile.

scrubber.description: Named scrubber applied before upload. Required even when classes is empty, so "no diagnostics captured" is an explicit statement.

capabilities.description: One entry per capability this profile requires the environment to prove before activation. Every category above (paths, commands, environments, network, identities, effects, resources) that this profile declares non-trivial policy for should have a matching capability entry here for the Capability Gate to check.

capability.description: A stable, exact, human-readable capability name, e.g. "network.exact-allowlist-externally-enforced". Named exactly so a missing capability produces a named Safety Blocker, never a generic failure.
